Released on 2026-10-31. Barn 0.x releases use GitHub's pre-release channel.

Barn 0.9.3 focuses on safer lab changes and recovery. It adds resource-only
resize, lets selected nodes converge independently, accepts ordinary user path
forms for inventories and shares, and makes interrupted lifecycle operations
recoverable. The release embeds signed image catalog revision `2026102802`.

## Changes

- **Resize without recreation.** Edit `vm_cpu` or `vm_mem` and run
  `barn resize [node...]`. Supported increases are hot-plugged when QEMU has
  reserved capacity; decreases, older VMs, and unsupported backends use an
  automatic stop/start. The VM identity, disks, SSH keys, and other settings
  remain in place. Image, disk, network, and share changes still use
  `barn recreate`.
- **Select the nodes to apply.** `plan`, `up`, `reload`, `recreate`, and
  `resize` retain the applied definitions of unselected peers. A changed or
  temporarily omitted peer does not have to be applied in the same operation.
  The complete inventory is still parsed, and address, alias, control-node,
  and deployment-wide conflicts are rejected before a node is stopped or
  deleted. `reload` refuses changes that require `resize`, `recreate`, or
  `destroy` before it stops anything.
- **Choose an image in generated templates.** `barn init [template] --image`
  and `barn setup [template] --image` write an alias, channel, or version
  selector to `all.vars.vm_image`. They do not download an image and cannot
  rewrite an existing inventory selected with `-f` or discovery.
- **More usable paths and shares.** `BARN_HOME`, local repositories, catalog
  export, `BARN_MAC_RUNNER`, inventories, imported images, and share sources
  accept relative paths, `~/`, and directory symlinks where applicable.
  Inventory-relative share sources resolve beside the inventory's real file.
  Share sources may contain spaces, Unicode, and shell punctuation; readable
  directories do not need to be owned by the caller, and multiple guests may
  share overlapping trees. Guest mount paths and shell/fstab values are
  normalized and quoted safely. Output-file symlinks are still protected from
  overwrite.
- **Larger and safer image workflows.** Local images and catalog artifacts with
  declared sizes no longer have an 8 GiB limit. Imports are indexed by content
  digest, so source names with spaces or Unicode and identical bytes are safe;
  the local alias registry has no 256-entry ceiling and rejects oversized
  updates before changing the existing registry. Cache and catalog checks keep
  enforcing declared size, SHA-256, and qcow2 structure, and pruning protects
  images referenced by applied nodes and local aliases.
- **Provisioning and logs.** `barn provision --parallel` accepts any positive
  value and `--timeout` accepts any positive duration. `barn mac logs --lines`
  accepts any positive line count, including logs beyond the former 1 MiB and
  10,000-line limits. Fallback loopback port allocation uses every valid
  `+10000` candidate.
- **Embedded image catalog.** The release embeds signed catalog revision
  `2026102802`, covering 9 distribution families and 17 architecture-specific
  artifacts. The default remains Ubuntu 24.04 (`u24:stable`) on the host's
  native architecture; run `barn image list` to inspect the active catalog.
- **Recovery and readiness.** Interrupted Linux and macOS lifecycle, persistent
  disk, and replacement operations retain enough journaled state for the next
  command to recover safely. `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` cancel active operations
  with the structured `cancelled` result. On macOS, `barn mac up --no-wait`
  now explicitly returns when the VM process starts; first-boot SSH and sudo
  provisioning may still be running, so run `barn mac up NAME` again before
  using `mac ssh` or `mac exec`.

## Upgrade

Select **0.9.3** explicitly with the download installer, or upgrade the
Homebrew formula / Linux package. GitHub's `releases/latest` does not select
pre-releases. Existing Linux and macOS VM disks, credentials, and configuration
remain under `~/.barn`; no recreation is required for this upgrade.

```bash
curl -fLO https://github.com/pgsty/barn/releases/download/v0.9.3/install.sh
BARN_VERSION=0.9.3 bash install.sh
```

After upgrading, run `barn update` if you want to activate the current remote
catalog for a repository. The embedded catalog is already available in the
binary; catalog activation never upgrades the Barn executable or replaces a
running VM's disks. Keep an explicit `vm_image: family@version` when a lab must
remain on one exact image across catalog updates.

The 0.9.3 macOS arm64 archive and Homebrew installation continue to provide
the signed, notarized `Barn.app`, CLI, and hosts helper from one release. Stop
macOS VMs before replacing the native component. Linux arm64/amd64 and Intel
macOS continue to provide the CLI and hosts helper; Linux guests use QEMU.

See the [installation guide](https://barn.pgsty.com/docs/start/installation/),
the [Linux quick start](https://barn.pgsty.com/docs/start/tutorial/), and the
[Mac guide](https://barn.pgsty.com/docs/start/macos/) for platform-specific
instructions.
